The mark "06" means that that was the civilian tasks sector under Colonel Milos Djurdjic. All correspondence that was sent to UNPROFOR, most of the time would be logged in our logbooks marked as 06.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We are talking about helicopter flights, and before that we were talking about medical evacuations. I would like to show you 5D1298. In this document, we see that a medical evacuation has been approved for February 14, 1995, to evacuate a sick child accompanied by his twin brother and mother. This document is dated 13th of February --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is an interpretation problem in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Because in English we are receiving interpretation for sure. Let's start with the accused, first. Were you receiving interpretation in your language? No. So there is a problem for sure. I don't need to ask anyone else. Could I have an indication of when the interpretation into B/C/S stopped? In other words, what needs to be repeated. THE ACCUSED MILETIC: [Interpretation] The last question, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the specific question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will read it out myself slowly. Madam Fauveau's questions was the following: "We are talking about helicopter flights, and before that, we were talking about medical evacuations. I would like to show you Exhibit number 5D1298. In this document, we see that the medical evacuation has been approved for February the 14th, 1995, to evacuate a sick child accompanied by his twin brother and mother. This document is dated 13th of February." That's where you had stopped. I don't think that concluded your question, so if you could proceed and bring it to an end, then the witness can answer assuming that it all has been now interpreted into B/C/S. Okay. Go ahead, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: My question is the following: How long did it usually take for such requests to be decided upon?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of the helicopter flights is a very sensitive one. As far as actions by units are concerned, if they were not informed about these helicopter flights. That means that it was necessary after receiving approval of information to send an act to the corps command or, rather, to units on positions that at a certain time the corridor would be opened, and the helicopter flights would be approved referring to the precise route in order to prevent any incident happening that may mean the downing of the helicopter. So that warning would imply a reasonable period of time of at least six hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: My question was: When you receive a request for a medical evacuation of that sort, how much time was it necessary to decide at the level of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evacuations had priority. Such a document would immediately be processed in the shortest possible way. It would need to reach General Mladic or General Milovanovic quickly in order to complete the process as soon as possible, and you could see from the document itself that nature of the injury, whether it was an evacuation that could maybe take some time, or whether it was necessary to do it immediately. But it would be processed in the shortest possible time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would be a good moment to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Merci, Madam. Let's have the break now, 25 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were speaking of the helicopter missions; in particular, this mission approved for the 14th of February, 1995. Could the witness be shown 5D1126. Now, this is a report from the Main Staff 14th February 1995. Could the witness be shown page 3 in English and B/C/S. It's page 3 in both cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this first paragraph, I am talking about item 6 (a), we can read that in the area of the 5th and 6th Brigade, Podrinje, a helicopter which had not been announced and which is not yet identified as been seen. Do you know which region was covered by the brigades of Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area leading up to the protected areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We see that helicopter had been approved. Now, in this report -- by the report, can you conclude that it is indeed the helicopter -- the helicopter which had been approved or is it another helicopter?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not about an approved helicopter. It is about a helicopter of unknown origin using the corridor to carry out a mission of its own. Knowing very well that during that time, no fire would be opened.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown document 1299. This is a document sent by the Main Staff to UNPROFOR. In the second paragraph, I can see that the helicopter mission which had been approved took place without any problem, but that after that in the sentence beginning by -- at 11.30, one sees that another helicopter was heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to know if such incidents had an influence on the decisions taken by the Main Staff concerning the approval of helicopter missions?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the monitoring of such incidents provided the Main Staff with an opportunity to pay special attention to the approvals granted to helicopter missions, which means that there was analysis and most missions were requested to use the land route, if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We spoke of the UNPROFOR convoys and the medical evacuations. Could you tell us who in 1995 decided that are humanitarian convoys could pass, could go through?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decisions were made by the commander or the Chief of Staff if they were about the movement on UNPROFOR. And the coordination body provided appropriate approvals and proposals to the Main Staff to consider convoys of humanitarian organisations in the part dealing with the transport of such supplies which might be used for the other side's military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could document 5D1283 be shown to the witness, and this is an intercept which, unfortunately, has no date. But by the contents of the conversation, it's obvious that it was July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this conversation, one of the speakers takes place, and it is supposed that it is Colonel Djurdjic who took part. But what I am interested in is what is said about state committee which decided to approve the requests of HCR, UNHCR, 1418 and 1428 and 1429. Would you know what this organ is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government had established a committee to cooperate with humanitarian organisations. Its seat was in Pale. The president of that committee was the vice-president, Vice-president Koljevic, and Colonel Djurdjic represented the Main Staff as a member of that committee. The committee to cooperate with international humanitarian organisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could document 6D7 be shown to the witness. In B/C/S that's page 2, while in English it's page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You can see there it's about a decision of the creation of the state committee for cooperation with the United Nations and the international organisations dealing in humanitarian matters, and I would like you to look at Article 5, which is on page 2 in the English text. The first organ we see mentioned in this article is the coordination organ for humanitarian operations. We have already several times seen this coordination organ mentioned. Does this decision have to do with this coordination we already spoke about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who would send the requests for the passage of convoys, of humanitarian convoys, to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the coordination body from the secretary's office, they would send it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1284. This is a conversation or an intercept. The date is not determined.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And do you know when Colonel Djurdjic arrived at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Djurdjic took over from Colonel Magazin. I arrived -- or, rather, joined on the 3rd of November, 1984 [as interpreted]. He was already there. I can't give you the exact date. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you repeat which year this was. When did you arrive at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take over any duties. I joined. Colonel Djurdjic was still in his position, and I joined on the 3rd November 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this conversation, Colonel Djurdjic speaks with a certain Branko or Branka, and he says that requests have to be sent by the -- through the coordination organ. And what I would like to know is if you look at what you've got at the bottom of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in English it's the beginning of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Colonel Djurdjic speaks about the official procedure and of a rectangular stamp. What -- do you know what Colonel Djurdjic is talking about in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the regular procedure that was used in the coordination body. Before this body existed, some other organisations sent their requests directly to the Main Staff. This is obviously a Branka from the area of Sarajevo to whom they sent assistance through the Main Staff. And, now, since the new organisation was in place, they were supposed to talk to the coordination body, and they did not have enough information; and it was Branka's intention to try and push this through to Colonel Djurdjic . However, Colonel Djurdjic was performing according to the new procedure that was put in place. He clearly told her that it could not be sent for the procedure if it did not go through the procedure of the new coordination body.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1308. And could page 2 in B/C/S be displayed and page 3 for the English version, please. We can see there is a stamp, a rectangular stamp on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you explain what it is, this rectangular stamp?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a stamp of the coordination body, the body that we have just discussed. And this is a list of their documents, and you can see clearly the title of the body, the Coordination Body for Humanitarian Aid, whose president was Vice-president Koljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go back to back to page 1 of the document. We see that this is a document from the coordinating body dated 17th of May, 1995; and I am interested in the note we see on this document at the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It says that the weekly plan was approved except for note 3 on page 3, satellite telex with equipment needed for the UNHCR office. Who decided that this equipment could not go through?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coordination body decided that. The coordination body of the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is number 1179-HCR-783 dated 17th of May, 1995. I'd like to show you another document, 5D905. Here we have a notification from the Main Staff. The date is a bit difficult to decipher, but I believe it's the 18th or the 19th of May. Here in the first paragraph of this document, we read: "We hereby notify you that we have approved request number 1179-HCR-783 of the coordinating body."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn to page 2, please. The very bottom of the page, we have a note here saying we have not approved the transport of a satellite telex to Srebrenica on the 24th of May with accompanying equipment. This is the next-to-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When the Main Staff received documents from the coordinating body, what was the procedure then followed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Colonel Djurdjic was a member of the Coordination Body for Humanitarian Aid of the government of Republika Srpska, when he received a document of this nature, he was clear that the coordination body had informed UNHCR that the equipment would not be allowed to pass. And according to the regular procedure, he informed his superior officer, in this case either General Mladic or General Milovanovic, who did not have any objections to this type of document. They simply approved it automatically. However, this obviously so far as a technical mistake. It says in the remark: "We did not approve the transport of satellite telex with equipment to Srebrenica, even before the coordination body had informed UNHCR about that and told them that this would not be approved." There was no need to put this into the remark to subordinated units. For the subordinated units, it would have sufficed that the order had arrived from the Main Staff and the convoy escort had been provided by a written document from the coordination body disallowing this type of transport.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You stated that it was not necessary to send that to subordinated units, but how would subordinated units know what was approved and what was not approved if that particular information was not disclosed to them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It seems to me that this is not a sufficiently clear question. What the witness testified to was the remark on the document referring to "we did not approve it," and the question that's being put to him is not in that context. It's in a completely different context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment to that? I think Mr. Vanderpuye is right. But it's up to you, Madam, if you think your question is right you can pursue it, and we'll see then what the witness has to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would the coordination body send its direction -- its decisions directly to the corps and to the brigades?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1405. I believe that this document should not be displayed outside of this courtroom. It's an intercept that has not been translated. We have prepared a draft translation. Whilst the document is being brought up, one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Kekic is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kekic was a member of the coordination body.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5D1405, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. While we're waiting for that one to come up, I just wonder if my colleague could put on the record which collection this particular exhibit comes from so that the record is clear as to what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, are you in a position to do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Let's move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are we back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a report dated 8th of June, 1995. I would like to have page 2 of this document displayed, please. This is an intercept -- or the conversation starting at 1758 [Realtime transcript read in error, "1959"] mention is made of Lieutenant Kralj, or a Lieutenant Kralj. Later on in that conversation, we see that you first spoke with colonel -- or Major Basevic and then with a colonel whose name has not been recorded properly. During that conversation you say that Kekic was wondering what was going on with the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you find that portion of the intercept?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: A few lines further down, you say he's the main person of the Republika Srpska, the man in charge for Republika Srpska when it comes to humanitarian transfers?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters don't have translation in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you find this portion of the intercept? It's a few lines down.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the document in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did Kekic have a specific role when it came to humanitarian aid and its transport?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was involved in the work of the government coordination body.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn to page 2 of this document, please -- or page 3, sorry. Page 3 in B/C/S. Third line.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You say, "He approves, he does not check or control." Who you are referring to here?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coordination body does not inspect the convoys. It approves the convoys. So this refers to the coordination body.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we return page 2, please. The bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I believe that you read this portion of the intercept?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify for the record, at page 56, line 3, the time of the intercept is recorded in the record as "1958" it should be "1758." And I believe the date isn't recorded in the record, I wonder if you might put that on since I don't have it in front of me just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Prosecutor is right. The time is 1758 and the date is 8th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I believe that you've already read the portion of the intercept I want to discuss with you now. There is something here about ammunition apparently found in the convoy. Do you remember such cases? I am not talking about this particular case, but I am talking about similar situations.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were instances when ammunition that was not reported was being transported. The procedure was that such a convoy could not be allowed to pass to the other side and to urgently inform the Main Staff as well as the humanitarian body, the humanitarian coordination body.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1259. This is a regular combat report from the 1st Podrinje Brigade dated 8th of June, 1995. Could you please turn to item 3 of this document. It relates to a convoy that was bound for Zepa but that is still in Rogatica because it's undergoing a detailed search since ammunition has been found in the convoy. This is a report from the Podrinje Brigade to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Was the Drina Corps under the obligation to notify the Main Staff of such incidents?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regular procedure was to inform of the passage of convoy. The corps would do that. They would inform the Main Staff and if there was an incident, a more detailed report would be required separate from the regular daily report.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D856. We talked about UNHCR weekly plans. Here we have an authorisation or, rather, an approval for the weekly plan approved by the coordination body. This is a document dated 12th of May, 1995. Could you please turn or have a look at the destination of these convoys, Bijeljina, Visegrad, Vlasenica, Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On which territory were these places located? Were they located in Republika Srpska or on the territory of the federation?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first convoy, Sremska Raca, Bijeljina, Karakaj, Vlasenica, is the territory of Republika Srpska. The second convoy, Sremska Raca, entrance to Republika Srpska, Bijeljina, Karakaj, Vlasenica, all of these places are in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: These convoys going to Republika Srpska, was their passage to be announced as well in advance?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was announced regularly with a public text via fax through our office, by fax through our office.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would the convoys going to Republika Srpska be in a position to pass or to go through without having been authorised?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing could pass the checkpoint if it was not approved.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What about the inspection of convoys bound for Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure was the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will need an additional 20 minutes tomorrow morning, so I was wondering if the time was not the right one to stop for today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no problem with that. It's almost quarter to 2.00 in any case. So we adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the morning, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Kralj, we have to stop here today. We'll continue tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. We'll make an effort to finish tomorrow, because otherwise you will be staying here Saturday, Sunday, and Monday; Monday being a public holiday for the UN. So we'll try and make an effort, please, tomorrow to finish with this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
